title: A safer start on Intel Macs

items.text: Intel Macs: if the game dies in its first 90 seconds, the next start switches to the OpenGL renderer by itself and stays on it. This is a fallback for a crash one tester hit, and it has not been confirmed on an Intel Mac yet.
OpenGL on a Mac: the floor and the outdoor ground asked for more textures than a Mac's OpenGL allows, so they did not draw. They now use a lighter version there.
OpenGL on a Mac always runs with the Performance mode values.
A start that dies while loading now sends its log on the next launch, so crashes like this one report themselves.

title: Blade and gun work together, and two machines that want your blade

items.text: Gun marks: a hit from your gun marks a machine for 4 seconds (an amber pip by its health bar). Your next blade hit on it lands as a finisher, with double the posture, and uses the mark up. Shoot into a pack, then cut.

Three legendary powers for blades only. Serrated Arc: each cut on a machine makes your next cuts on it 10% stronger, up to five. Breaker Pulse: a parry bursts outward and hits, slows and unbalances every machine within 4.5 m. Reaping Stroke: an execution carries half its blow to every other machine within 4 m.

The Bulwark, from depth 2: a walker behind a plate of amber light. The plate turns three quarters of any shot or power that meets it from the front. Your blade goes straight through, and so does anything from behind. Break its posture and the plate drops.
The Phase Drone, from depth 2: a drone with a violet lens that blinks aside when you shoot it. A blade hit pins it in place for a few seconds.

Intel Macs: the game no longer asks for an Apple silicon upscaler there, and the OpenGL renderer no longer logs a shadow error every frame. The crash at start on some Intel Macs is still being tracked down.

title: Healing from kills has a limit

items.text: Healing from kills (Bloodcoil, Hunger, the Void finisher and Leech Relay) now shares one limit that refills at 4% of your max integrity a second. One kill still feels good, but a horde can no longer keep you topped up. Executions heal outside the limit.
Players returning on an older cloud save with two guns now get a blade, so right click always does something.
With only a blade or only a gun, either mouse button or trigger uses it.

title: The workshop, a Blade skill tree and mastery

items.text: The workshop: use the workbench on the Nightjar and a bench opens beside your inventory. Put any weapon or armour on it to see it up close, then upgrade it, re-forge it, build a component from your parts and fit it, fit a mod from your bag, or salvage it.
A Blade skill tree, open to every alignment: Slipstream, Riposte, Keen Edge, Executioner, Iron Guard and Tempest.
Mastery: once every tree you can use is full, spare skill points buy small lasting bonuses to damage, integrity and Current, with no limit.
Skills you can learn now are tinted in their tree's colour, so open trees are easy to spot.
If the game catches a burst of a graphics error linked to white flashes, it turns particles off for the rest of the session and tells you.

title: Blade and gun, parries, executions and armour you can see

items.text: Two weapon slots: right click (RT) swings your blade, left click (LT) fires your gun, with no swapping. Everyone starts with a Worn Arc Blade.
Parry: raise your guard just as a blow or bolt lands to turn it aside, and your next swing is a sure critical hit.
Posture: blade hits fill a bar under a machine's health. When it breaks, swing near it to execute it with one huge blow.
Every blade hit has weight now: a short freeze, a camera kick and sparks, heavier for heavier stances. A dodge cancels a swing and keeps your place in the combo.
Healing: elites always drop a health canister and ordinary machines rarely do. Each heals 15% of your max health, and you walk over to pick it up.
Machines and crates drop salvage parts for the fabricator and reactor.
Your best armour piece shows on your outfit: steel at Rare, a gold edge at Epic, dark metal with an emerald edge at Legendary.
Hints now show the keys for the device you are using, including blade stance (Z on keyboard), guard, parry and execute. On controller, Skill moved to B.

title: The Nightjar in white and gold, a fabricator, and new sword moves

items.text: The Nightjar is rebuilt in clean white panels with gold trim: gold door arches, gold-edged deck tiles, columns at the panel joints and detailed wall tops. It is drawn at full resolution with its own even lighting.

Fabricator on the Nightjar: lasting upgrades bought with salvaged parts and credits. Companion plating, targeting and field kit, more bag and locker slots, and better salvage yields, three levels each.
Energy blade: hold the stance key to guard. Hits from the front land much softer and bolts are turned back. Let go after a moment for a charged strike down your aim line. A tap still changes stance.
Ask to join: press ASK next to a player in the players list (O). They answer yes or no on a banner, and a yes takes you straight into their party.

title: A rebuilt Nightjar and players who look like themselves

items.text: The Nightjar's interior is rebuilt: textured deck plates, banded gunmetal bulkheads, door frames on the spine and painted guide lines, in place of the flat white panels.
Other players now appear with their own body, skin, hair, hood and outfit colour. Before, everyone was drawn with your look.
Other players are warm coral on the map, in name tags, toasts and tracers, so they stand apart from green doors and objectives.

title: Salvage, the reactor and a launcher that keeps itself up to date

items.text: Salvage: break any item in your bag into parts (Alloy, Wiring, Fusion Cores, Crystal Shards). Rarer gear gives more, and found crystals finally have a use.
Salvage everything below Rare in one go at the workbench.
The reactor: the core in the Nightjar's engine room has six marks to install with parts and credits, raising your Current and how fast it returns.
The launcher shows what's new in a panel of its own, and updates itself from now on.
Your companion points out salvage and the reactor the first time they matter.
The extra Current from PIP-7's core is no longer lost when you die, and is given back if you lost it.

title: A companion who talks and shows the way

items.text: Your companion talks. On a new game it tells you who you are, walks you to the freight lift and explains firing, dodging, loot, the bag, the exit lift, crystals and skills, each once.
It leads: it walks ahead to the next objective, waits for you and comes back if you fall behind.
Combat call-outs for low health, elites, relay waves and drops.
Everyone has a companion now. You can still rename it in the pause menu.
The companion stays put when you only move the mouse, and stands behind the way you last walked.
The city has more to say: people standing around talk too, and what you hear follows your progress.
Particles setting: turn every particle effect off for more speed.

title: New blade moves

items.text: Blade lunge: swing right after a dodge to close the gap with a longer, harder strike.
Blade deflect: while the blade is moving it turns machine bolts back at whatever fired them.

title: Difficulty that follows each player

items.text: On a run floor your damage dealt and taken is matched to that floor. Gear far above the floor still hits harder, but no longer many times harder, and a player below it gets a little help. Stricter on Insane than on Normal.
Your companion deals a share of your matched damage, so it no longer clears a floor on its own.
The status line says MATCHED TO FLOOR when the floor is holding your damage back.
Co-op: each player's hits carry their own weapon bonuses, not the party leader's.

title: Shared loot, a steadier picture, guns that cool on their own

items.text: Co-op: loot is shared. Everyone in a party sees the same drops in the same places, and picking one up takes it for everyone. Credits and XP stay your own.
Co-op: a locker or case opened by anyone opens for the whole party, and either player can start the jam signal.
Each gun has its own heat. The one in your holster keeps its heat and cools there, with a second slim bar beside the first.
Combat particles setting: turn sparks, embers, smoke and dust off for more speed.
Other players carry their own weapon, and face the way they walk instead of twitching about.
The launcher notices a new version while it is open and installs it by itself. It also has a What's new button.
Flashes, giant glowing shapes on characters and missing shots and effects in big fights: the main cause is fixed, and far fewer should remain.
Machines no longer stay wedged against pillars and props.

title: Updates from inside the game, steadier co-op, less loot

items.text: A running game tells you when a newer version is out. RESTART AND UPDATE in the pause menu closes it, updates and starts it again.
Co-op: vault doors, relays, lockers, cases and coolant bays are in the same places for everyone in a party.
Players list: nobody can join your world without your invite.
Very crowded deep floors have more room for effects, so shots and blasts are less likely to go missing or draw wrongly.
Loot: a little less of it and far fewer Rare (yellow) drops, with more Uncommon and Epic.
Ordinary machines drop gear about one kill in 55 (was 40). A champion's second piece comes one time in five (was three), and champions no longer always drop Rare or better.
The jam signal is started by the party leader, so a party member can no longer skip its waves and still collect the payout.

title: See your party fight, a steadier picture on Mac

items.text: Co-op: you see other players shoot, with muzzle flashes and tracers along their aim.
The players list and the status line say whether you are in a party and who leads it.
Upscaling setting: Auto, Stable or Sharp.
Slipstream, a Prism skill that shortens the dodge cooldown.
Taking the lift to a depth a recent party member is already on puts you on their floor.
Armory: a weapon you take goes to your bag, and what you hold stays in your hands.
Dodge has a 1.6 second cooldown (was 0.55), with a small ring when it is ready again.
On a Mac the picture uses a steadier upscaler by default.
The Nightjar's wall panels and the city's street fronts and columns are solid, so nobody stands inside them.

title: Invite codes and an easier first launch

items.text: Invite codes: type a code in the launcher once and you are in. No account or email needed.
The launcher has a How to play button.
The game can report errors to help fix them.
First launch: the launcher starts the download by itself, says what it is getting and that Play comes next.
Inventory: an item's details sit beside the panel, always on screen, next to what you have equipped in that slot.
Inventory cards are nearly opaque and easier to read.
With another player in your world, opening a menu no longer pauses the game for everyone. Alone, it pauses as before.
Player names show the name you were invited as, or your computer's user name, instead of everyone on Windows being Pilot.

title: A new opening

items.text: The game starts on a fight: First Contract is the first quest, and its marker points at the freight lift.
Shore Leave, the tour of the ship and the city, opens after your first run as side work.
First Contract's last step, learning a skill, can be done anywhere.
Coming home from a run puts you back at the entrance you left by: freight lift, raid gate or deep shaft.

title: Arc Blade and legendary powers that change builds

items.text: Arc Blade, an energy sword. It drops as loot, sits in a weapon slot and is on the armory's close range rack.
Arc Blade stances on Z or the right stick: Light (a fast three-swing chain), Balanced (wide arcs that catch a group) and Heavy (two slow swings that stagger, then a slam).
The last swing of a chain is a finisher powered by your alignment: Radiant throws a wave of light and raises a ward, Void drains what it hits, and balance returns Current.
Eleven new legendary powers, 17 in all.
Overdrive, Glass Cannon, Momentum, Executioner, Shrapnel and Ward Engine change how you fight.
Sunforged, Afterimage, Long Reach and Resonance rebuild a skill around the weapon: a free Sunlance, Phase Step reset on a kill, Void Lash on three machines, a faster Kinetic Pulse.
Sweeping Edge, a legendary power for blades only.
Legendaries you already own keep the power they had.

title: Floor conditions and best times

items.text: Floor conditions: about two run floors in three roll a twist: Overclocked, Plated, Unstable cores, Rich seam, Champion nest, Current surge or Brittle.
The condition shows beside the depth and is announced when you arrive. Harder ones pay more XP or better finds.
Results show your best time for each tier's contract and raid.
Launcher: a new eclipse backdrop whose glow shows what it is doing: emerald when the game is ready, amber while checking or downloading, red when something failed.

title: Three ways down, a new Nightjar interior

items.text: Three ways down, in three parts of the city: contracts at the freight lift, raids from a raid gate and the endless depths from a deep shaft.
Each way down has its own lift platform and light colour, and the minimap points to each by name: CONTRACTS, RAIDS, DEPTHS.
The Nightjar's interior is rebuilt in white panels with gold trim, with windows on the hull walls, new shelves, consoles and capsules.
Grey squares no longer show through the Nightjar's floor.

title: Playing together

items.text: Players list on O and in the pause menu: who is online and where, with Invite beside each name.
Notices when a player comes online or goes down on a run.
The minimap always points to the way down and to every other player in the zone.
One press on another player invites them. An invite is a banner you answer with Y or N.
Wall lamps on run floors no longer glow as a bright slab through walls, and gunfire no longer makes the fog strobe.

title: Skill tree and raids

items.text: Skill tree on K and in the pause menu: three branches, three tiers and 18 skills.
Every level gives a skill point. Passives take three ranks, and each tier opens with points spent in its branch.
New passives: Vigour, Zeal, Reserve, Fleet, Focus, Ruin and Dread.
Raids: clear a tier's contract to open its raid. Five floors, a Relay Warden holding the lift on floor 3 and the Overseer on floor 5.
Raids pay more XP, better loot luck and 4 or 5 vault pieces.

title: Speak to chat

items.text: Hold V to speak a chat line. It is turned into text on your own computer and lands in the chat line for you to check; Enter sends it.
The speech model (57 MB) downloads once, the first time you use it.

title: Chat, parties and a new quest log

items.text: Chat: Enter opens a line, and everyone online sees it with your name and where you are. You stand still while typing.
Parties: walk up to another player in a safe zone to invite them. They answer yes or no and join you.
Quest log: cards in two columns with a progress bar, ticked steps, the current step in gold with where to go, and the reward.
A calmer city: fewer people on the streets, walking between real places and stopping a while when they arrive.
The landing pad is kept clear, nobody appears right next to you when you arrive, and passing remarks are rarer.

title: A living city

items.text: Port Halden has a crowd: people, service robots, sweepers, haulers, dock robots and drones, groups stopped to talk and people at the stalls.
Four street traders at stalls: noodles, weapon mods, surplus guns and drinks.
People far out of view stop animating, which saves frame time.
Sparks, steam vents and flickering lamps no longer flash inside the fog like lightning in a cloud.

title: Port Halden, the city

items.text: Port Halden is the hub: one city with the Nightjar on a landing pad, a market and the freight lift that starts every run.
Lifts from the depths bring you back up to the city, and quests point at the city and contract floors.
Street fronts built from sci-fi panels, with shopfronts at street level and windows lit warm, pale and emerald.
Roof decks, plazas with light masts and cargo stacks, a paved landing pad with landing lights and strings of bulbs round the market.
The city at night is easier to read, with lighter fronts and softer edges to the screen.
Towers between you and the camera are cut away, so they no longer black out part of the screen.

title: Much smaller updates

items.text: Updates come in parts and most are a few MB. The large art download only comes again when the art changes.
On a Mac the launcher opens straight away, with no unknown developer warning.

title: Windows

items.text: Singularity runs on Windows, with its own launcher.
HUD corners read as one block: each card is as wide as the cluster under it.
The way into contract runs is labelled, and until you clear Tier I a reminder says where it is.

title: City districts

items.text: Contract floors from Tier II up are city districts.
Launcher: Pause and Resume really pause and resume the download.

title: Contracts, levels and a companion

items.text: Contracts: three floors with the Foundry Overseer at the bottom, across five tiers. Clearing one opens the next.
A free supply cache on contract floors: pick one of three mods or an overclock.
Character levels and XP from kills and finished runs, with a level and XP bar top left.
A companion follows you, fights beside you, draws fire and gets back up 10 seconds after going down. Rename it in the pause menu, or switch it off in Gameplay settings.
HUD: health and the repair injector bottom left, Current and your abilities bottom right, the middle of the screen clear.
Dying on a run keeps your loot and half its XP, and you wake in Port Halden.
The death screen names the floor you were on, and the minimap shows the right depth after loading a save.

title: Less loot, more range, playtest fixes

items.text: Named wrecks can be boarded, and the lift back up returns you beside them.
The launcher has its own icon.
The map remembers what you explored, and area gates show where they go.
The camera sits further back, and machines only start fighting once they are on screen or close.
Smaller updates: the launcher downloads only what changed.
Station decks have new sci-fi wall panels with viewing windows and warm lamps.
Ordinary machines drop an item about one kill in 40 and never Common. Champions always drop one Rare or better piece.
Only Rare or better loot shows its label from afar; the rest shows within 5 metres.
Corridor hordes on Hard and up stop growing past depth 6.
The constant electric crackle is gone.
No T-pose behind the title screen.

title: The loot update, the launcher and a new look

items.text: The Singularity launcher installs the game, keeps it up to date and starts it.
Legendary weapons roll a unique power: Detonator, Leech Relay, Current Siphon, Elite Hunter, Static Charge or Ricochet.
Mods drop from machines at every rarity. Fit them from the bag or by dragging onto a weapon or armour piece.
Weapon affixes that reward a style: Tracker suite, Point-blank rig, Fracture rounds, Salvage loop and Harvest coil.
Containers on dungeon floors: lockers, weapon cases, medical cabinets, supply crates and fallen workers.
Special weapons: the Ricochet Disc Launcher and the Gravity Well Projector, both in the ship armory.
Character appearance: body, skin, hood, nine hairstyles, six hair colours, facial hair and outfit dyes.
17 new gun models. Fitted mods show on the gun, and Rare or better guns carry a sight.
Dungeon floors carry lab consoles, specimen capsules, cargo and breakable crates.
Frame rate on deep floors is much higher (about 30 to about 49 fps at depth 18 on a fast Mac). Default render scale is 0.6.
A new HUD and inventory in gunmetal and emerald, with bigger ability slots and large cooldown numbers.
Item and character pictures lose their black boxes.
Readouts hold up on bright ground, and your character stands out from it.
New colours across the game: tech glows go emerald, Radiant goes gold and Prism green.
Launcher downloads can be paused, resume after a restart and retry by themselves after a dropped connection.
Machines never start a fight within 12 metres of the arrival lift.
Reinforcement waves stop growing past depth 6, though machines still get tougher.
The Relay Warden's enraged barrage is lighter.
Dodging no longer turns you into a white ghost.
On a controller, the d-pad in the inventory no longer swaps weapons.
